newsitem.title: USA: Cooper Industries settles securities suit.
newsitem.headline: Cooper Industries settles securities suit.

text.p: Cooper Industries Inc said Tuesday it has agreed to pay $6.85 million into a fund as part of a settlement of a class action securities lawsuit.
The lawsuit, which dates back to 1994, will have no effect on the company's financial results, it said. The agreement is subject to court approval.
The lawsuit was brought against the company and certain current and former officers on behalf of all of Cooper's stockholders.

The lawsuit centered around the company's public announcement on January 25, 1994, that the deterioriation of oil, gas and other energy-related markets could cause the company's share earnings to decrease by as much as 25 percent in 1994.
Cooper said it denies the material allegations of the lawsuit and admits no liability. It said it agreed to the settlement to avoid the expense and distraction of further legal proceedings.
Cooper did not immediately return a telephone call.
Cooper manufactures electrical products, tools and hardware, and automotive products.
The stock dropped dramatically after the earnings warning, and the suit was filed shortly after.

When asked if he believed the stock's drop was exaggerated by the earnings warning, a spokesman said, "I couldn't speculate on the stock's reaction after the news and we issued the statement as a part of our fiduciary responsibility."
